reasons: The logic is short and the design is explained in comments.
No test is visible in the packet to confirm the fingerprint moves when the contract changes.
The current function depends on a module that is not shown here.

terms.meaning: A standard method that turns any text into a fixed-length code, so that any change to the text changes the code.
A short code that identifies the shape of something, so two shapes can be compared quickly.
A standard written description of the shape a JSON record must have.
The outer labels of a schema document, such as where it is published, as opposed to the content of the record.

depends_on: Python standard library hashlib and json

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Purpose and stripped labels
sections.what: Explains why the fingerprint exists and lists the labels removed before hashing: descriptions, titles, examples and the schema identifier fields. Nothing a user sees is produced here directly.
sections.why: The docstring says prose is removed so rewording a sentence does not force a version bump that people would then stop taking seriously.
sections.watch_out: The version and identifier fields must stay out of the hash, or the fingerprint would follow the version instead of checking it.

sections.name: structural
sections.title: Removing prose from the schema
sections.what: Walks through the schema and removes the prose labels at every level, keeping list order, so the remaining structure reflects field names, types, required fields and allowed values.
sections.why: The docstring says list order carries meaning, such as the order of allowed values, so sorting lists would hide real changes.
sections.watch_out: Sorting any list here would let two different contracts produce the same fingerprint.

sections.name: fingerprint
sections.title: Computing the hash
sections.what: Converts the stripped schema to text with keys in alphabetical order and no extra spaces, then returns the first sixteen characters of its SHA-256 hash.
sections.why: Sorted keys mean that reordering field declarations in code does not move the hash, since that does not change what stored records look like.
sections.watch_out: Sixteen characters is a short code, so it is a change detector, not a security guarantee.

sections.name: current
sections.title: Fingerprint of the current build
sections.what: Loads the record model's live schema and returns its fingerprint, so the running code can be compared with the declared version.
sections.why: Likely reason: it lets a test compare the live contract with a stored value without copying the schema by hand.
sections.watch_out: It imports the record module when called, so calling it during module loading could cause a circular import.

summary: Creates a short hash of the shape of the record contract, so a change to the contract cannot go unnoticed when the version number is not bumped.
purpose: Makes a silent change to the stored record format visible as a changed fingerprint rather than a confusing validation error later.
why: The docstring explains that a forgotten version bump causes failures only when old stored records are read back, and the fingerprint catches that earlier.
how: First, the record schema is taken from the record model. Second, descriptions, titles, examples and envelope keys are removed at every level. Third, the rest is serialised to text with keys sorted. Fourth, the SHA-256 hash of that text is cut to sixteen hexadecimal characters. The current function fetches the live schema and returns its fingerprint.
inputs: A schema dictionary, usually the JSON schema of the record model.
outputs: A sixteen character text fingerprint. The current function returns the fingerprint for the running build.
risks: Removing a key from the stripped list would make prose edits move the hash. Keeping an item that changes with the version would make the check always agree with itself.
debug: If the fingerprint changes unexpectedly, compare the structure before and after with descriptions removed. If the current function fails, check that the record module can be imported without a circular import.
